description:
FOUND by s540c (s541 resume, 2026-11-13) running tools/t/sbcl-floor.t on its tree while its own 2.6.0 legs (sweep,
Path-Tiny one-file runs) ran on the same tree.  A TOOLS hazard, not a runtime bug.

tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm, after a successful build (lines ~350-354):
    for my $old (glob("\Q$dir\E/pcl-$pathkey-*.core")) {   # this runtime's older cores
        unlink $old unless $old eq $core;
    }
The pathkey is per runtime PATH; the content key hashes `sbcl --version` too.  So a 2.5.2 core and a 2.6.0 core of
the SAME tree are each other's "older cores": building either deletes the other.  Two runners on two SBCLs then
ping-pong (each spawn of the side whose core is gone rebuilds it, ~1 min under load, and deletes the other's), and a
spawn whose `--core X' was computed before X was deleted fails at once (rc 1, empty stdout) -- e.g.
Pl/t/tap-exit-01.t computes its prefix ONCE and spawns 19 programs: under SBCL 2.5.2 it failed 3 of 4 runs on the
s540c tree (rows 11-37 in one run, 23-39 in another) and 0 of 3 on a base extraction (whose path no 2.6.0 run used),
and 0 of 32 in a serial loop once the 2.6.0 legs were over.  Observed directly: at 22:36 the tree had a 2.5.2 core
(pcl-964abe6a-a2cd87702868.core); at 22:40 only a new 2.6.0 one (c4a7c0fd1b43, built 22:39:55) existed.

Who meets it: anyone running tools/t/sbcl-floor.t (PCL_SBCL_FLOOR) or the container leg on a tree that other runners
use at the same time -- an agent's worktree during its legs, main during the round.
Fix sketch: delete only older cores of the same SBCL VERSION (put a version tag in the name, or read it from a
sidecar), or keep the newest core per (path, sbcl --version).  Guard: build a core under each of two `sbcl' binaries
for one runtime path and assert both files exist (tools/t/sbcl-prefix.t is the file for it).
subject: tools: building a core DELETES the other SBCL version's core of the same runtime path -- a floor (2.5.2) run beside a 2.6.0 run of the same tree makes spawns fail with no output (tap-exit-01.t 3 of 4 under sbcl-floor.t)
